collectionunit.notes: “The Supulah North Pond was discovered and a core collected on the southern edge by Simon Haberle in May 1987, at which time it contained more than 2 m of water. The section consisted of 200 cm of fine black peat over brown clay. The water level had dropped to about 1 m on returning in January 1991 (the original core having been lost by the Australian Quarantine Inspection Service). Access to the centre of the basin allowed a 352 cm core to be extracted. Difficulty was  experienced in penetrating a layer of brown humic sands." -(Hope, 1998)

site.sitedescription: "Supulah Hill is about 5 km north of the town of Wamena on the eastern bank of the Baliem River, and is the largest ridge breaking the basin plain. This ridge, and a parallel ridge 2 km to the north, Siobara Hill, are elongate  structural features about 2 km in length. Today it is completely deforested, grassy, with numerous tracks crossing past  rocky outcrops. A few shrubs of Vaccinium sp. Rhododendron  maius (J.J. Smith) Sleumer, R. sp. and Baeckia sp. grow  in sites sheltered from fire, and a possibly introduced  Grevillea sp. is spreading. Three basins, each 30-50 m across, contain water in which sedges are growing. The northernmost basin was chosen for coring."-(Hope, 1998)
